text:
I've read the entire codebase — 5 source files plus tests and config. Here's my honest assessment.

## Overall

This is **good code**, and I want to say that plainly rather than manufacture problems to match a "it's rough" expectation. It's cleanly structured, fully type-annotated, uses frozen/slotted dataclasses sensibly, has a coherent retry/backoff design, typed exception hierarchy, and a test suite that exercises the genuinely tricky parts (pagination, 207 partial-failure aggregation, batch chunking with index preservation, retry-after, idempotent review). Codex did a competent job here.

The issues I found are real but almost all minor — polish and robustness, not correctness landmines. There is no data-corrupting bug, no credential leak, no broken core path.

## Concrete issues

| # | File | Line(s) | Sev | Issue |
|---|------|---------|-----|-------|
| 1 | lumen/client.py | 172, 195, 224, 241 | medium | Path params (`project_id`, `task_id`, `annotation_id`) interpolated into URLs without `urllib.parse.quote` — IDs with `/`, `..`, or special chars are not escaped. Low real risk (server-issued IDs) but it's the only thing touching a security boundary. |
| 2 | lumen/client.py | 81 | low | `response.status_code < 400 or response.status_code == 207` — the `== 207` branch is dead; 207 is already `< 400`. |
| 3 | lumen/client.py | 93-95 | low | Code after the retry loop is only reachable when `max_attempts < 1`; `_raise_for_response` is typed `-> None`, so `_request` has no `NoReturn` guarantee and a type checker sees an implicit `None` return. |
| 4 | lumen/client.py | 105-109 | low | `Retry-After` only parsed as numeric seconds; the HTTP-date form is silently ignored (falls through to backoff). |
| 5 | lumen/client.py | 77-91 | low | Only HTTP status codes are retried; `httpx.TransportError`/timeouts propagate immediately and are never retried, despite README implying robust retry handling. |
| 6 | lumen/client.py | 167-168, 228-229 | low | Pagination breaks only on `next_cursor is None`; an empty-string cursor (`""`) would loop forever re-fetching page one. |
| 7 | lumen/client.py | 242 | low | `review()` always sends `"note": null` when no note is given, rather than omitting the key. |
| 8 | lumen/models.py | 54, 88, 151 | low | `status`/`state`/`verdict` are typed as `Literal[...]` but passed through from the payload unvalidated — runtime accepts any string. |
| 9 | lumen/models.py | 4 | low | Uses deprecated `typing.Mapping`; client.py correctly uses `collections.abc.Mapping`. Inconsistent. |
| 10 | lumen/models.py | 115, 66 | low | `from_dict` validators (`confidence`/`priority`) raise `ValueError` mid-pagination — a malformed API row throws a non-`LumenAPIError`, surprising for callers catching the typed hierarchy. |
| 11 | tests/test_client.py | — | low | Coverage gaps: no test for 5xx/exponential-backoff path, 404→`NotFoundError`, non-JSON/non-object response handling, or model validation. |

## Lines to rewrite

Small. These are targeted edits, not a structural rewrite — roughly **20–30 lines** changed/added (URL-encoding helper, drop dead branch, `NoReturn` annotation, cursor guard, conditional `note`, optional literal validation), plus a handful of new test cases.

## Bottom line

**Yes — I'd approve this in a PR**, with the above left as non-blocking review comments (item #1 being the one I'd most want addressed before merge). Nothing here is a release blocker. Bringing it back into active development is safe; the fixes are cleanup, not rescue.
